adjudications.why: Solver read the 46% case as a one-year bar (answer 4: A and B); NTA's final key is option 1 (A, B and C). The 2018 regulations bar a Level 2 student from submitting a revised script for one year, after which a revised script is submitted, so NTA's reading is defensible; the solver's is the more literal one. Two defensible answers: key kept, notice, grace (owner policy 2026-10-29).
adjudications.solution:
The UGC (Promotion of Academic Integrity and Prevention of Plagiarism in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2018 set four levels of similarity for a thesis:

- Up to 10%: **Level 0**, minor similarity, no penalty.
- Above 10% up to 40%: **Level 1**, the student must submit a **revised script** within six months.
- Above 40% up to 60%: **Level 2**, the student is debarred from submitting a revised script for one year, and then submits the revised script.
- Above 60%: **Level 3**, the registration for the programme is cancelled.

So a revised thesis is submitted at 12% and 27% (Level 1) and, after the one-year bar, at 46% (Level 2). At 66% and 70% (Level 3) the registration is cancelled, so no revised thesis is possible.

That gives A, B and C. So the answer is option (A).
adjudications.notice: NTA's final key gives option (A), counting the 46% case because a Level 2 student submits a revised thesis after a one-year bar. Read strictly, only Level 1 (12% and 27%) leads straight to a revised thesis, which is option (D). In our mock tests everyone gets this question's marks.
